# 0031. A typed AuthFacade client is generated by NSwag from a committed OpenAPI snapshot

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-10-31
- **Builds on:** [0019](0019-token-endpoint-binds-typed-form-parameters.md), [0021](0021-token-form-is-a-request-dto-with-attribute-validation.md), [0022](0022-binder-failures-return-a-bare-400.md)

## Context

Before building a real frontend against AuthFacade, something needs to call its API in a typed way rather
than hand-rolling `HttpClient` calls. Two real options were weighed:

- **NSwag**, generating a C# client from the existing OpenAPI document (`Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi`,
  already configured by `AuthFacadeOpenApi.cs`).
- **Kiota**, Microsoft's own newer generator, or hand-written `HttpClient` wrappers.

NSwag was chosen: it is the most mature option for this document shape (form-urlencoded request bodies,
not just JSON), and reuses a document AuthFacade already produces, rather than adopting a second generator
alongside the OpenAPI pipeline already in place.

Generating the client turned out to need two further decisions, both found by actually trying to make the
generated client work end to end, not by reading NSwag's docs alone.

**Where the OpenAPI document comes from.** The obvious approach — `Microsoft.Extensions.ApiDescription.Server`,
generating the document at build time with no server running — was tried first and rejected. That tool
genuinely runs the app's startup (confirmed: the stack trace goes through `Host.StartAsync` and
`StartupValidator.Validate()`), and AuthFacade's startup requires `OpenEmr:ClientId` and `OpenEmr:ClientSecret`
(`OpenEmrOptions`, both `[Required]`), which are deliberately never committed to any file — only injected via
`.env`/Docker (`docker-compose.yml`). Making `OpenApiGenerateDocumentsOnBuild` unconditional would have broken
every plain `dotnet build` of the Api project for everyone, not just whoever regenerates the client.

**Whether a generated client can actually complete a login.** Once a smoke test tried the generated client
against a real running instance (reusing `TestApi`, the same in-process host the existing unit tests already
use), the password grant failed with `400 invalid_request` — not a tooling bug, a real gap in AuthFacade. See
Decision 3.

## Decision

1. **`OpenEmrNext.AuthFacade.Client`**, a new class library project, holds the generated client. It has no
   `ProjectReference` to the Api project; the OpenAPI document is a file, not a build artifact of it.
2. **`scripts/dev/generate-authfacade-openapi.sh`** regenerates the committed snapshot
   (`OpenEmrNext.AuthFacade.Client/OpenAPIs/AuthFacade.json`) by actually running AuthFacade briefly — the
   same way a developer would with `dotnet run` — with placeholder values for `OpenEmr:ClientId`/`ClientSecret`
   (`openapi-codegen-placeholder`, the same kind of stand-in `TestApi.cs` already uses for its own tests, not
   a real secret), reading `/openapi/v1.json`, then stopping it. `OpenEmrNext.AuthFacade.Client.csproj`'s
   `OpenApiReference` points at that committed file with `CodeGenerator="NSwagCSharp"`, so every ordinary
   build only ever reads a static file — no server, no secrets, no dependency on build order.
3. **`TokenRequest` now normalizes an empty optional field to `null` before any attribute validation runs**
   (`Username`, `Password`, `RefreshToken` — not `GrantType`, which is unconditionally required). The record
   was converted from positional syntax to an explicit constructor so this normalization has somewhere to
   run; the `[FromForm]`/`[JsonPropertyName]`/validation attributes are unchanged in substance, just moved
   from parameter position to property position.
   - **Why this was a real bug, not a client-generation quirk.** `POST /api/v1/connect/token` has one shared
     form for two grant types (ADR 0019/0021): which fields are *required* depends on `grant_type`
     (`TokenRequest.Validate`), but every field's `[StringLength(..., MinimumLength = 1)]` applied
     unconditionally, regardless of grant type. A generated client has no way to omit the field its chosen
     grant type does not use — it serializes one DTO with all four properties — so it sends the irrelevant
     field as `""`, and `[StringLength(MinimumLength = 1)]` rejects an empty string even though it already
     accepts `null`. The same failure would hit a refresh-grant call sending empty `username`/`password`, or
     any other client that submits a field it has no value for as `""` rather than omitting it outright —
     this was already a real gap before NSwag ever entered the picture, just never exercised, because every
     existing caller (the integration tests, a real browser form) happened to omit the irrelevant field
     instead of sending it empty.
   - **Why normalize, not just relax the attributes.** Dropping `MinimumLength = 1` (and loosening
     `Username`'s regex to allow zero length) would have also started accepting a *literal* empty string as a
     valid value for the field that *is* required for the chosen grant type, which is wrong — `Validate()`'s
     own `IsNullOrEmpty` check needs that case to still read as missing. Normalizing first means validation
     only ever sees `null` or a genuinely non-empty value, so the existing required-field checks (and the
     documented `minLength` in the OpenAPI schema) stay exactly as strict as before.
   - **Confirmed safe for the endpoint handler**, not just the validator: `TokenEndpoints.cs`'s `switch` on
     `GrantType` only ever constructs the domain value object for the branch it takes (`new Username(...)`,
     `new Password(...)` for the password grant; `new RefreshToken(...)` for the refresh grant) — the
     irrelevant field, now `null` either way, is never passed to a value object that would reject it.

## Consequences

- `OpenEmrNext.AuthFacade.Client` has no ProjectReference to the Api project and needs none rebuilt to
  build; it only goes stale if the Api's OpenAPI shape changes without someone re-running the script. There
  is no automated drift check yet — a future CI step comparing the live document to the committed one would
  close that gap; not built here.
- The smoke test (`AuthFacadeClientTests`) is the first test in this project that proves a *generated*
  client, not just the raw HTTP surface, works against the real pipeline. It is also incidentally the thing
  that caught the `TokenRequest` gap — a concrete case for "test against a real round trip" (this project's
  existing habit, see ADR 0026/0027/0029) paying off again.
- `TokenRequest`'s own tests (`TokenRequestTests.cs`) gained two cases locking in the new behavior: an empty
  irrelevant field is accepted and normalizes to `null`, for both grant types.
- Any other request DTO that shares the same "one form, requiredness depends on another field" shape would
  have the identical latent gap; this ADR fixes `TokenRequest` specifically, not the validation pipeline in
  general (`RequestValidationExtensions` stays a generic, unopinionated filter) — a future DTO with the same
  shape needs its own normalization, not inherited from this one.

## Alternatives considered

- **Build-time document generation** (`Microsoft.Extensions.ApiDescription.Server`). Rejected; see Context.
- **Kiota or hand-written `HttpClient` wrappers.** Rejected for now: NSwag already fits the existing OpenAPI
  pipeline and the form-urlencoded shape; revisit only if NSwag's own maintenance status becomes a concern
  (it issued a deprecation warning for the now-removed `Microsoft.Extensions.ApiDescription.Client` package
  reference during this work, though `NSwag.ApiDescription.Client` alone built cleanly without it).
- **Relaxing the validation attributes instead of normalizing.** Rejected; see Decision 3.

## Related decisions

Builds on [0019](0019-token-endpoint-binds-typed-form-parameters.md) and
[0021](0021-token-form-is-a-request-dto-with-attribute-validation.md) (the typed, attribute-validated form
DTO this ADR amends) and [0022](0022-binder-failures-return-a-bare-400.md) (bare-400 binder failures, the
behavior that made the real cause of the generated client's failure non-obvious until traced directly).
Precedes the MudBlazor frontend work this client was scaffolded for, which has not started.
